contexts: 16-bed medical and surgical intensive care unit
lean facilitator four hours a week
reading: The morning process has three hand-offs: the screen, the decision to stop sedation, and the breathing trial. Local data show the loss after the screen (71 to 38 percent) and after the interruption (38 to 29 percent). The retrieved records point to waits for authority and to poor coordination with respiratory therapy rather than to forgotten screens, and a reminder that improved documentation left practice unchanged. Fear of self-extubation drives nurse decisions, although self-extubation is rare.
